SAMPLE SRD-STYLE SOURCEBOOK (synthetic fixture, not a real RPG product)
=======================================================================

This file is hand-authored synthetic content shaped to look like a tabletop
RPG sourcebook for the purposes of testing the theme-extraction pipeline.
No real RPG IP is reproduced here. Use this fixture in unit tests; for
end-to-end smoke against actual sourcebooks, point the operator command at
a real PDF outside the repo.

Setting Overview
----------------

The realm of Verdant Hollow is a windswept patchwork of moorland, fen, and
old growth forest, ruled in name by the Council of Mossy Tor but in practice
by whichever Lordmagus has paid the corvée this season. The tone is wary
and folkloric; people speak in proverbs and check the road over their
shoulder. Magic is older than the Council, polite to no one, and arrives
through bargains rather than spells.

Core Mechanic
-------------

Resolution uses a single d12 plus the relevant Aspect rating, against a
Reckoning set by the Hollowmaster. Ties go to the player. Critical
successes occur on a natural 12; critical failures on a natural 1. There
are no degrees of success in this system; success is success.

Actions and Common Verbs
------------------------

When a hero strikes in combat, we call it a swing. When they ward themselves
or another, that is a holding. To press an opponent or NPC for information
or a deal is to barter. To inspire allies is to call the chorus. To study a
clue or environment is to read the omen. To slip past notice is to walk
unseen. To use a craft or trade is to ply the trade. Movement of any kind
is a stride.

Factions and Personae
---------------------

The Council Warden carries a wax-sealed warrant and a heavy oak baton.
They speak quietly, kindly, and entirely without warmth — a person used to
having the last word in a conversation that no longer feels like a
conversation.

The Hedgewitch travels light, with a satchel of dried herbs, a glass-eye
fetish, and a chipped iron knife. Their demeanor is brisk, practical, and
unimpressed by titles. They prefer payment in kind.

The Lordmagus-At-Arms is imperious, armored in lacquered plate and a
high-collared cloak. They carry a long pistol cast in three metals and a
court-sealed dueling parchment. They have not been refused since they were
a child.

The Tor-Shepherd is weather-creased and patient, carries a curved staff,
a flock-counter of carved bone, and a clay flute. They speak in old proverbs
and rarely without good reason.

The Drowned-Mason is a journeyman returned from places that should have
drowned them. They carry a brass plumb-line, a cracked compass, and a
sketchbook of impossible architecture. Their demeanor is unhurried; their
quietness has weight.

Scene Atmosphere
----------------

Scene introductions in Verdant Hollow lean on weather, soundscape, and
small uncomfortable details: the wet smell of peat smoke, a lapwing
calling somewhere too close to the door, a candle that gutters when no one
is breathing on it.

Combat begins with stillness, then noise. Crows lift from the trees in a
single shape. Steel clears leather. A breath later, no one is where they
were.

Rest scenes are spare. The hearth ticks. Someone is sharpening something
in another room. The night outside the window is honestly dark.

Victory looks like a careful inventory: who is still standing, what is
ruined, what can be carried away before the road takes notice. The
landscape does not celebrate.

Defeat looks like a long walk back, knowing the Council will hear about it
before you do.
